identity.name: BAJEL PROJECTS LIMITED
identity.industry: Power T&D EPC — High-Voltage Transmission Lines & Substations (765 kV-class) + captive tower/monopole manufacturing

summary.oneLiner: Bajel Projects Limited is a Bajaj Group power infrastructure EPC specialist with over two decades of experience, executing high-voltage transmission, monopole, and emerging energy projects while pivoting toward quality-of-earnings and scalable growth under its RAASTA 2030 strategy.
summary.business: Bajel Projects Limited provides engineering, procurement, construction, testing, and commissioning services across power transmission, new energies, monopoles, and emerging adjacencies like data centers and battery storage. The company serves utilities, transmission developers, and industrial clients in India and select international markets, leveraging its Ranjangaon manufacturing facility for backward integration. It operates as a distinct listed entity following its demerger from Bajaj Electricals Limited in 2023, drawing on the governance standards of the Bajaj Group.

currentContext.strengths: High-voltage and extra-high-voltage execution prowess with extensive pre-qualification and high barriers to entry|First-mover advantage in monopole technology for space-efficient urban infrastructure, resolving right-of-way challenges|Process-driven scalability through Project Neev, institutionalising digital project monitoring, mechanised erection, and real-time dashboards|Efficient working capital management that allows supply chain and customer advances to finance growth while minimising interest-bearing debt|In-house design capabilities aligned with specialised manufacturing for superior cost control and total vertical integration|Selective global footprint with depth-over-breadth strategy via strategic joint ventures combining execution with regional market presence|Digital project governance enhancing project predictability and transparency to mitigate delivery risks|Strategic pivot to high-growth sunrise segments including data centres, metros, and battery energy storage
currentContext.strategies: Focus on expanding international business presence through dedicated senior leadership.|Strengthen supply chain management and in-house manufacturing capabilities.|Drive corporate social responsibility programs through a dedicated committee and policy framework.|The Dividend Distribution Policy aims to balance rewarding shareholders through dividends and retaining earnings for sustained growth. The Board considers external factors (economic conditions, market trends, taxation, industry payout ratios) and internal factors (distributable surplus, liquidity, capital requirements, borrowings, contingent liabilities) when declaring dividends. Shareholders may not expect a dividend under adverse market conditions, inadequate profits, high working-capital needs, large forthcoming capital requirements, or changing regulations, though the Board retains discretion to recommend a dividend even in such circumstances.|The Corporate Social Responsibility Committee oversees CSR policy, programs, budgets, and performance, with two meetings held in FY 2025-26 to review strategic frameworks and community relations.|The Risk Management Committee is mandated to identify, assess, mitigate, and monitor risks including cybersecurity and financial risks, and to periodically review the risk management framework.
currentContext.expansion: During FY26, the Company incurred capital expenditure of ₹37.56 crore, primarily towards property, plant and equipment, capital work-in-progress, and other intangible assets. As of March 31, 2026, gross fixed assets stood at ₹195.43 crore. The Company continues to focus on judicious management of working capital and cash flows to support its business requirements. No specific new capacity expansion projects with commissioning timelines were disclosed.

risks.risk: Execution and project delivery risk in large-scale EPC contracts
risks.note: As a power transmission and distribution EPC company, delays, cost overruns, or quality issues on complex projects can materially impact profitability and reputation.

risks.risk: Concentration risk from dependence on a limited number of large clients or geographies
risks.note: Revenue concentration with key customers or regions exposes the company to significant financial impact if a major client delays or cancels orders.

risks.risk: Working capital intensity and liquidity risk
risks.note: The business requires substantial working capital for inventories and receivables; any strain on cash flows or tightening of credit could constrain operations and growth.

risks.risk: Regulatory and policy risk in the power sector
risks.note: Changes in government policies, tariff regulations, or delayed approvals for power transmission projects can adversely affect order inflow and project execution.
Intense competition in the EPC space may lead to aggressive bidding, compressing margins and making it difficult to secure profitable orders.
The company relies on a small senior management team; the departure of key executives (e.g., CFO change in 2025, CS/Compliance Officer change in 2026) could disrupt strategic continuity.

risks.risk: Supply chain and raw material price volatility
risks.note: Fluctuations in prices of steel, copper, and other inputs can erode project margins, especially for fixed-price contracts without escalation clauses.

one-line thesis: Pure-play 765 kV transmission EPC carve-out from Bajaj Electricals, pivoting from scale-led to quality-led growth — record >INR1,000 cr quarter, 100 bps FY26 EBITDA-margin lift, strong order inflow (+55% YoY) and first MENA win, but absolute margins still thin (~4.4%) and exposed to commodity/working-capital swings.
financial scorecard (standalone):
| Metric | Q4 FY26 | YoY | FY26 | YoY | Notes / one-offs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | INR1,008 cr | +26% | INR2,792 cr | +7% | First-ever >INR1,000 cr quarter |
| EBITDA / margin | INR38 cr / 3.7% | +39% (margin +30 bps) | INR125 cr / 4.4% | +38% (margin +100 bps, from 3.4%) | from INR90 cr FY25 |
| PAT | INR16 cr / 1.6% margin | — | INR27 cr / ~1% margin | +74% | FY26 hit by labor-code exceptional INR7.72 cr; PBT-before-exceptional INR42 cr (+73%) |
| Order book (unexecuted) | — | — | INR3,442 cr (31-Mar-26) | — | Order inflow FY26 ~INR3,100 cr vs ~INR2,000 cr (+55%) |
| Other | — | — | Net D/EBITDA 2.8x; NWC 124 days; ROACE 15.8% (+300 bps); cash borrowings INR31 cr (vs INR121 cr) | — | Maiden dividend INR0.60/sh (30% of FV INR2); finance cost ~INR63 cr FY26 |

*Note: Q4 EBITDA margin 3.7% was a sequential DIP — prior quarter was ~4.8% — driven by commodity spike (aluminum/steel/zinc/copper all up).*
guidance (next year — fy27):
- **Revenue growth: "upwards of 15%"** for FY27 ("quite confident we should get there"); explicitly NOT chasing top line, but acknowledges scale needed for fixed-cost absorption.
- **Order book target: INR4,000–5,000 cr unexecuted by end-FY27.**
- Margin: aim to protect/improve via hedging, in-sourcing, Project NEEV; customers being approached for relief on extraordinary commodity moves.
- Tone: "cautiously optimistic" entering FY27 given US-Iran conflict / MENA slowdown.
order book & pipeline:
- Unexecuted OB INR3,442 cr (31-Mar-26). FY26 inflow ~INR3,100 cr (+55% YoY).
- Key FY26 wins: INR700 cr TBCB from MSETCL (400/220 kV substation + line, Saswad); PGCIL Mandsaur project; PGCIL Vindhyachal pool project.
- Post-March: >INR1,000 cr secured in first ~40 days of FY27, including **first MENA order ~INR400 cr** (500 kV overhead line).
- L1 / advanced negotiation: >INR2,000 cr. Active pursuit pipeline: **INR22,000 cr.**
- FY26 execution: commissioned 17 projects, 1,168 ckm (~10% of India's total transmission-line addition in FY26).
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Tripartite SPV (Bajel + NIIF + AnantGrid):** announced 10-Mar-26. Bajel takes a SMALL equity stake (analyst cited ~26%); financing largely by NIIF/AnantGrid. Bajel gets back-to-back EPC contracts and is contractually EXITED at commissioning — explicitly NO long-term asset ownership / no O&M. Mgmt frames it as pipeline-quality enhancement and access to marquee LPs (CPP, ADIA-type sovereigns).
- **KSA JV (50:50 with Al Sharif):** long-term MENA platform.
- **5 employee-welfare trusts:** mark-to-market loss INR6.67 cr (FY)/INR1.57 cr (Q4) due to weak end-March equity prices; expected to reverse as markets recover — not a recurring operating item.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **HVDC:** NOT yet in portfolio but "keen" to add; fully qualified up to 765 kV (both GIS & AIS) so credentials no longer a constraint — waiting for the right opportunity.
- **Monopoles:** dedicated new line (phase 3) — mgmt sees high future demand and claims design + manufacturing edge.
- International: GCC/MENA/Africa (Saudi Vision 2030, UAE, Oman, Egypt) — selective, well-priced 500 kV tenders.
- RAASTA 2030: six-year roadmap — high-voltage complex EPC, selective profitable international, margin via digitization (Project NEEV), adjacent infra.
margins & cost dynamics:
- FY26 EBITDA margin 4.4% (+100 bps); Q4 3.7% (sequential dip vs ~4.8% prior qtr).
- Exposed to aluminum, zinc, steel, copper. Aluminum largely hedged through FY26 (some open exposure on new orders); steel/zinc effectively un-hedgeable.
- Steel rose post safeguard-duty imposition; depreciating INR added pressure.
- Margin levers: in-sourcing tower/monopole (lower COGS), Project NEEV digitization, disciplined bidding, customer price relief talks.
capex / expansion:
- **Ranjangaon (near Pune) expansion: total capex INR170 cr** — capacity 45kt → 110–120kt p.a. (~2.5x). Funded INR120 cr term loan + INR50 cr own funds.
- Phase 1: large galvanizing bath ready by August 2026 (bulk of spend this year).
- Phase 2: TLT capacity 2,000 → 6,000 MT/month — ready end-FY27 / early FY28.
- Phase 3: new monopole line — by end-FY28. Phases 1+2 ≈ 60–70% of capex.
- Rationale: in-source captive tower/monopole demand amid market-wide supply tightness (solar/wind competing for tower capacity), protect margins & execution control.
capital allocation:
- Maiden dividend INR0.60/share (30% payout on FV) — commemorates Bajaj Group centenary + first profitable signal.
- Deleveraging: cash borrowings INR121 cr → INR31 cr; net D/EBITDA to 2.8x.
- Capex (INR170 cr) part debt-funded (INR120 cr term loan).
- SPV equity kept deliberately small — capital-light EPC stance, no asset ownership.
risks & watch-items:
- Thin absolute margins (~4.4% EBITDA, ~1% PAT) — vulnerable to commodity/execution slippage.
- Commodity inflation (Al/steel/zinc/copper); steel & zinc unhedgeable; crude >$100, LPG shortage, FX depreciation.
- **Working capital:** debtors up INR590 cr (INR1,258→INR1,849 cr); NWC 124 days. Mgmt attributes to higher Q4 billing (+INR194 cr), one marquee customer holding ~INR225 cr in late March (since largely collected), and rising EPC retention (+~INR100 cr) — claims one-time, mostly recovered.
- US-Iran conflict slowing MENA ramp; manpower/skilled-labor shortage; new labor code raising costs.
- FY26 ordering "temporary moderation" industry-wide on capacity/bandwidth.
management quality / tone:
- Inaugural call after >2 yrs listed — improving disclosure/IR posture. Chairman framed around Bajaj 100-yr legacy ("Kathni Karni Ek Si").
- Candid: openly flagged Q4 margin dip, commodity exposure, working-capital spike with specific numbers; directly addressed a skeptical retail question on SPV EPS dilution. Repeatedly stressed quality-over-scale and capital-light discipline. Credible, measured, "cautiously optimistic."
non-obvious takeaways:
- The SPV is structured to be EPS-accretive, not dilutive: tiny equity, back-to-back EPC, exit at commissioning — a pipeline-sourcing device, not an asset play.
- "Quality-led growth" = deliberately capping top-line ambition (15%) while prioritizing margin/working-capital — a re-rating could come from margin, not revenue.
- In-sourcing capex is as much a supply-security play (tower capacity scarce as solar/wind compete) as a cost play.
- Fully 765 kV qualified (AIS+GIS) — HVDC is the only remaining capability gap, and they're actively hunting it.
- The INR225 cr marquee-customer withholding and trust MTM loss are non-structural — reported PAT understates underlying.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary stock(s) | Loser | Why / conviction |
|---|---|---|---|
| India INR9 lakh cr transmission capex to 2032 (~INR1 lakh cr/yr); 900-1000 GW non-fossil by 2036 | BAJEL · 544042 (self) | — | Multi-year, well-funded grid-capex supercycle; Bajel 765 kV-qualified pure-play. High conviction (sector tailwind), low on near-term margin capture. |
| Renewable integration → grid stabilization bottleneck (T&D, not generation) | BAJEL · 544042 (self); KEC International (code unverified); Kalpataru Projects Intl (code unverified) | — | Inter-regional transfer + RE evacuation drives EHV/HVDC line ordering. Med conviction. |
| Tower/monopole supply scarcity (solar/wind competing for capacity) | BAJEL · 544042 (self — Ranjangaon in-sourcing) | EPC peers reliant on third-party towers (code unverified) | Captive 110-120kt capacity gives cost + supply-security edge. Med conviction. |
| MENA/GCC 500 kV grid expansion (Saudi Vision 2030) | BAJEL · 544042 (self — KSA JV, first INR400 cr win) | — | New export leg; but US-Iran conflict slowing ramp. Med-Low conviction near term. |
| Commodity inflation (Al/steel/zinc/copper), unhedgeable steel/zinc | — | BAJEL · 544042 (self) — margin compression | Q4 margin dipped to 3.7%; only aluminum hedgeable. Med conviction on margin drag. |
| Working-capital / receivable stretch in PSU-heavy T&D EPC | — | BAJEL · 544042 (self) — debtor days, borrowings | NWC 124 days; debtors +INR590 cr; mgmt says largely one-time/collected. Low-Med conviction (transient). |
qoq change log:
**This quarter (Q4/FY26):**
- First-ever >INR1,000 cr quarter (Q4 rev INR1,008 cr, +26% YoY); FY26 rev INR2,792 cr (+7%).
- FY26 EBITDA margin +100 bps to 4.4%; but Q4 margin DIPPED to 3.7% (vs ~4.8% prior qtr) on commodity spike.
- Maiden dividend INR0.60/sh declared. Inaugural earnings call held.
- Order inflow +55% YoY (~INR3,100 cr); OB INR3,442 cr. MSETCL INR700 cr TBCB win.
- NIIF/AnantGrid tripartite SPV + Al Sharif KSA 50:50 JV signed.
- Ranjangaon INR170 cr expansion announced (45kt→110-120kt).
- Labor-code exceptional INR7.72 cr; trust MTM loss INR6.67 cr (FY).

**Next-quarter / FY27 watch items:**
- Verify FY27 revenue tracks the "15%+" guide and OB closes at INR4,000-5,000 cr.
- Galvanizing bath commissioning by August 2026 (phase 1); watch capex pace (bulk this year).
- Conversion of INR2,000 cr L1 and INR22,000 cr pipeline; further MENA orders despite US-Iran drag.
- Margin recovery from 3.7% — does hedging / in-sourcing / customer relief restore the trajectory?
- Working-capital normalization (collection of withheld receivables, debtor-day trend).
- Any HVDC order entry — the stated capability gap.

themes.title: Power transmission & renewable-evacuation capex
themes.need: Grid build-out to evacuate ~90 GW of new renewables is the broadest theme in the universe - pulling EHV/765kV transmission EPC, towers, conductors, OPGW, cables and HVDC. POWERGRID/ADANIENSOL TBCB pipeline plus state RDSS/underground-cabling capex (Rajesh Power 544291, OMPOWER) underpins multi-year visibility for EPC, tower (KP Green 544150, SKIPPER) and conductor/cable makers (KEI, RRKABEL, DYCL).
themes.driver: Fresh TBCB awards + execution ramp; EPC order inflows over next 1-2 quarters.

one_liner.body: Bajel Projects Limited is a Bajaj Group power infrastructure EPC specialist with over two decades of experience, executing high-voltage transmission, monopole, and emerging energy projects while pivoting toward quality-of-earnings and scalable growth under its RAASTA 2030 strategy.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Bajel Projects Limited provides engineering, procurement, construction, testing, and commissioning services across power transmission, new energies, monopoles, and emerging adjacencies like data centers and battery storage. The company serves utilities, transmission developers, and industrial clients in India and select international markets, leveraging its Ranjangaon manufacturing facility for backward integration. It operates as a distinct listed entity following its demerger from Bajaj Electricals Limited in 2023, drawing on the governance standards of the Bajaj Group.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- **Tripartite SPV (Bajel + NIIF + AnantGrid):** announced 10-Mar-26. Bajel takes a SMALL equity stake (analyst cited ~26%); financing largely by NIIF/AnantGrid. Bajel gets back-to-back EPC contracts and is contractually EXITED at commissioning — explicitly NO long-term asset ownership / no O&M. Mgmt frames it as pipeline-quality enhancement and access to marquee LPs (CPP, ADIA-type sovereigns).
- **KSA JV (50:50 with Al Sharif):** long-term MENA platform.
- **5 employee-welfare trusts:** mark-to-market loss INR6.67 cr (FY)/INR1.57 cr (Q4) due to weak end-March equity prices; expected to reverse as markets recover — not a recurring operating item.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Power Transmission:** Transmission lines up to 765 kV, AIS/GIS substations, Transformers, Underground cabling
- **Monopoles:** Monopole towers for urban infrastructure
- **New Energies & Adjacencies:** Data Centre infrastructure, Battery Energy Storage Systems, Industrial Power solutions, Metro & Railways electrification

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- India (domestic power T&D, urban infrastructure, industrial power)
- Select African markets (EPC projects)
- More than seven countries (product supply)
- Saudi Arabia (via 50:50 JV for HV/EHV EPC)

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body:
- Unexecuted OB INR3,442 cr (31-Mar-26). FY26 inflow ~INR3,100 cr (+55% YoY).
- Key FY26 wins: INR700 cr TBCB from MSETCL (400/220 kV substation + line, Saswad); PGCIL Mandsaur project; PGCIL Vindhyachal pool project.
- Post-March: >INR1,000 cr secured in first ~40 days of FY27, including **first MENA order ~INR400 cr** (500 kV overhead line).
- L1 / advanced negotiation: >INR2,000 cr. Active pursuit pipeline: **INR22,000 cr.**
- FY26 execution: commissioned 17 projects, 1,168 ckm (~10% of India's total transmission-line addition in FY26).

guidance.title: Guidance (next year — FY27)
guidance.body:
- **Revenue growth: "upwards of 15%"** for FY27 ("quite confident we should get there"); explicitly NOT chasing top line, but acknowledges scale needed for fixed-cost absorption.
- **Order book target: INR4,000–5,000 cr unexecuted by end-FY27.**
- Margin: aim to protect/improve via hedging, in-sourcing, Project NEEV; customers being approached for relief on extraordinary commodity moves.
- Tone: "cautiously optimistic" entering FY27 given US-Iran conflict / MENA slowdown.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **HVDC:** NOT yet in portfolio but "keen" to add; fully qualified up to 765 kV (both GIS & AIS) so credentials no longer a constraint — waiting for the right opportunity.
- **Monopoles:** dedicated new line (phase 3) — mgmt sees high future demand and claims design + manufacturing edge.
- International: GCC/MENA/Africa (Saudi Vision 2030, UAE, Oman, Egypt) — selective, well-priced 500 kV tenders.
- RAASTA 2030: six-year roadmap — high-voltage complex EPC, selective profitable international, margin via digitization (Project NEEV), adjacent infra.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body:
- FY26 EBITDA margin 4.4% (+100 bps); Q4 3.7% (sequential dip vs ~4.8% prior qtr).
- Exposed to aluminum, zinc, steel, copper. Aluminum largely hedged through FY26 (some open exposure on new orders); steel/zinc effectively un-hedgeable.
- Steel rose post safeguard-duty imposition; depreciating INR added pressure.
- Margin levers: in-sourcing tower/monopole (lower COGS), Project NEEV digitization, disciplined bidding, customer price relief talks.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Maiden dividend INR0.60/share (30% payout on FV) — commemorates Bajaj Group centenary + first profitable signal.
- Deleveraging: cash borrowings INR121 cr → INR31 cr; net D/EBITDA to 2.8x.
- Capex (INR170 cr) part debt-funded (INR120 cr term loan).
- SPV equity kept deliberately small — capital-light EPC stance, no asset ownership.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: During FY26, the Company incurred capital expenditure of ₹37.56 crore, primarily towards property, plant and equipment, capital work-in-progress, and other intangible assets. As of March 31, 2026, gross fixed assets stood at ₹195.43 crore. The Company continues to focus on judicious management of working capital and cash flows to support its business requirements. No specific new capacity expansion projects with commissioning timelines were disclosed.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body:
- Inaugural call after >2 yrs listed — improving disclosure/IR posture. Chairman framed around Bajaj 100-yr legacy ("Kathni Karni Ek Si").
- Candid: openly flagged Q4 margin dip, commodity exposure, working-capital spike with specific numbers; directly addressed a skeptical retail question on SPV EPS dilution. Repeatedly stressed quality-over-scale and capital-light discipline. Credible, measured, "cautiously optimistic."

litigation.title: Litigation & compliance (profile)
litigation.body: {"material": false, "note": "No material litigation disclosed in the provided annual report sections.", "as_of": "2026-07-17"}

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- High-voltage and extra-high-voltage execution prowess with extensive pre-qualification and high barriers to entry
- First-mover advantage in monopole technology for space-efficient urban infrastructure, resolving right-of-way challenges
- Process-driven scalability through Project Neev, institutionalising digital project monitoring, mechanised erection, and real-time dashboards
- Efficient working capital management that allows supply chain and customer advances to finance growth while minimising interest-bearing debt
- In-house design capabilities aligned with specialised manufacturing for superior cost control and total vertical integration
- Selective global footprint with depth-over-breadth strategy via strategic joint ventures combining execution with regional market presence
- Digital project governance enhancing project predictability and transparency to mitigate delivery risks
- Strategic pivot to high-growth sunrise segments including data centres, metros, and battery energy storage

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- Thin absolute margins (~4.4% EBITDA, ~1% PAT) — vulnerable to commodity/execution slippage.
- Commodity inflation (Al/steel/zinc/copper); steel & zinc unhedgeable; crude >$100, LPG shortage, FX depreciation.
- **Working capital:** debtors up INR590 cr (INR1,258→INR1,849 cr); NWC 124 days. Mgmt attributes to higher Q4 billing (+INR194 cr), one marquee customer holding ~INR225 cr in late March (since largely collected), and rising EPC retention (+~INR100 cr) — claims one-time, mostly recovered.
- US-Iran conflict slowing MENA ramp; manpower/skilled-labor shortage; new labor code raising costs.
- FY26 ordering "temporary moderation" industry-wide on capacity/bandwidth.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- The SPV is structured to be EPS-accretive, not dilutive: tiny equity, back-to-back EPC, exit at commissioning — a pipeline-sourcing device, not an asset play.
- "Quality-led growth" = deliberately capping top-line ambition (15%) while prioritizing margin/working-capital — a re-rating could come from margin, not revenue.
- In-sourcing capex is as much a supply-security play (tower capacity scarce as solar/wind compete) as a cost play.
- Fully 765 kV qualified (AIS+GIS) — HVDC is the only remaining capability gap, and they're actively hunting it.
- The INR225 cr marquee-customer withholding and trust MTM loss are non-structural — reported PAT understates underlying.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Focus on expanding international business presence through dedicated senior leadership.
- Strengthen supply chain management and in-house manufacturing capabilities.
- Drive corporate social responsibility programs through a dedicated committee and policy framework.
- The Dividend Distribution Policy aims to balance rewarding shareholders through dividends and retaining earnings for sustained growth. The Board considers external factors (economic conditions, market trends, taxation, industry payout ratios) and internal factors (distributable surplus, liquidity, capital requirements, borrowings, …

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary stock(s) | Loser | Why / conviction |
|---|---|---|---|
| India INR9 lakh cr transmission capex to 2032 (~INR1 lakh cr/yr); 900-1000 GW non-fossil by 2036 | BAJEL · 544042 (self) | — | Multi-year, well-funded grid-capex supercycle; Bajel 765 kV-qualified pure-play. High conviction (sector tailwind), low on near-term margin capture. |
| Renewable integration → grid stabilization bottleneck (T&D, not generation) | BAJEL · 544042 (self); KEC International (code unverified); Kalpataru Projects Intl (code unverified) | — | Inter-regional transfer + RE evacuation drives EHV/HVDC line ordering. Med conviction. |
| Tower/monopole supply scarcity (solar/wind competing for capacity) | BAJEL · 544042 (self — Ranjangaon in-sourcing) | EPC peers reliant on third-party towers (code unverified) | Captive 110-120kt capacity gives cost + supply-security edge. Med conviction. |
| MENA/GCC 500 kV grid expansion (Saudi Vision 2030) | BAJEL · 544042 (self — KSA JV, first INR400 cr win) | — | New export leg; but US-Iran conflict slowing ramp. Med-Low conviction near term. |
| Commodity inflation (Al/steel/zinc/copper), unhedgeable steel/zinc | — | BAJEL · 544042 (self) — margin compression | Q4 margin dipped to 3.7%; only aluminum hedgeable. Med conviction on margin drag. |
| Working-capital / receivable stretch in PSU-heavy T&D EPC | — | BAJEL · 544042 (self) — debtor days, borrowings | NWC 124 days; debtors +INR590 cr; mgmt says largely one-time/collected. Low-Med conviction (transient). |

qoq_log.title: QoQ change log
qoq_log.body:
**This quarter (Q4/FY26):**
- First-ever >INR1,000 cr quarter (Q4 rev INR1,008 cr, +26% YoY); FY26 rev INR2,792 cr (+7%).
- FY26 EBITDA margin +100 bps to 4.4%; but Q4 margin DIPPED to 3.7% (vs ~4.8% prior qtr) on commodity spike.
- Maiden dividend INR0.60/sh declared. Inaugural earnings call held.
- Order inflow +55% YoY (~INR3,100 cr); OB INR3,442 cr. MSETCL INR700 cr TBCB win.
- NIIF/AnantGrid tripartite SPV + Al Sharif KSA 50:50 JV signed.
- Ranjangaon INR170 cr expansion announced (45kt→110-120kt).
- Labor-code exceptional INR7.72 cr; trust MTM loss INR6.67 cr (FY).

**Next-quarter / FY27 watch items:**
- Verify FY27 revenue tracks the "15%+" guide and OB closes at INR4,000-5,000 cr.
- Galvanizing bath commissioning by August 2026 (phase 1); watch capex pace (bulk this year).
- Conversion of INR2,000 cr L1 and INR22,000 cr pipeline; further MENA orders despite US-Iran drag.
- Margin recovery from 3.7% — does hedging / in-sourcing / customer relief restore the trajectory?
- Working-capital normalization (collection of withheld receivables, debtor-day trend).
- Any HVDC order entry — the stated capability gap.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
